claims.text: W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr are low-activation refractory elements.
Uniform incorporation of Ta, Ti, V, and Zr with W creates significant lattice distortion in equimolar WTaTiVZr.
Uniform incorporation of the constituent elements stabilizes a fine-grained microstructure in equimolar WTaTiVZr.
The combined lattice distortion and fine-grained microstructure enhance dislocation mobility.
The combined lattice distortion and fine-grained microstructure delay crack initiation relative to coarse-grained pure tungsten.
The reference equimolar WTaTiVZr HEA is homogenized, whereas commercially used pure tungsten has a standard coarse-grained microstructure.
The WTaTiVZr microstructure has enhanced grain-boundary cohesion.
Lattice distortion promotes a fine and thermally stable grain structure in equimolar WTaTiVZr.
The fine, stable grain structure facilitates additional active dislocation slip systems.
Additional active dislocation slip systems delay crack nucleation.
Pure tungsten tends to undergo grain coarsening and brittle fracture at high temperatures.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater plastic strain before failure than pure tungsten under identical high-temperature loading.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr will absorb more mechanical energy before failure than pure tungsten under identical high-temperature loading.
Under plasma-facing-component service temperatures, deformation and fracture are dominated by thermally activated dislocation motion and grain-boundary effects.
General HEA theory supports roles for lattice distortion and grain stabilization.
